messages:
michael (support): Hey team — multiple customers hitting 5xx + connection timeouts to the hosted /v1/generate endpoint in us-west-2 since ~14:21 UTC. Support ticket numbers: #8243, #8247. Sample curl shows 502 and long connect times.

michael (support): sample curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"rw-medium","input":"hello"}' -v``` responds with `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and `upstream connect timeout` in logs.

laura (oncall): Thanks — I'm on it. Spinning up the normal warroom. Who's the runtime lead? @diego?

diego (runtime): oncall here. I'm seeing a surge of 504s from the ingress gateway to the hosted runtime pool. Connection reset and long queue times on the gateway -> runtime socket. Checking lb and egress.

sam (eng-sre): I can confirm Cloud LB health checks look fine, but Batcher queue depth for the us-west-2 pool shot from ~200->1800 requests/sec at 14:20. Autoscale didn't add nodes fast enough, some pods OOMed causing transient 5xx.

ashley (support): Customer impact: short generation jobs failing intermittently, some retry loops causing billing noise. I've set expectations with two customers that we're investigating and will provide ETA.

diego (runtime): Repro steps I ran: flood test (k=1000 concurrent small prompts) against a canary endpoint. Observed kernel stalls and `grpc: connection closing` in the runtime logs. Pasting snippet: ```[2026-03-16T14:22:04Z] WARN grpc: connection closing
[2026-03-16T14:22:05Z] ERROR runtime/batcher: failed to dispatch request: no free worker```

laura (oncall): Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle new hosted requests via the gateway rate-limiter for us-west-2 (reduce ingress QPS), 2) enable fallback routing to a different region (eu-west-1) for non-sensitive tenants, 3) temp increase of pool size if infra has spare GPUs. Which can we do fast?

sam (eng-sre): I can patch the gateway config to reduce max concurrent requests for that region and enable fast-fail for large payloads (5m). Will push in next 2-3min. Also scheduling an emergency scale for the dedicated runtime ASG but that takes ~6-8min.

diego (runtime): If we toggle prefix cache to be more aggressive we might reduce work, but that's riskier. I'm in favor of throttling + cross-region fallback for immediate relief. I'll also eject the two OOM pods and mark them unschedulable while we root-cause.

ops-bot: Deploy started by sam (eng-sre): gateway-rate-limit-adjustment/us-west-2 v2. ETA ~3m.

michael (support): Noted. I'll update tickets and send a short status to affected customers: "We're throttling to stabilize capacity; failures should drop in a few minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and credit info."

jen (product): Please capture which customers were routed to fallbacks and any changes that could affect SLAs. Product wants a short summary for the account team.

sam (eng-sre): Gateway patch applied. Early telemetry: 5xx rate down ~65% in last 2m. ASG scale action in progress.

diego (runtime): Ejected two pods with OOM sigs. New pods coming up. Kernel stalls in older driver version — I'm rolling a small runtime patch to reduce kernel prefetch which has helped before. Will signal when patched.

laura (oncall): Good progress. Assigning action items: 
- diego: runtime patch + root-cause (driver/kernel) and postmortem writeup (owner).
- sam: refine gateway throttles and add circuit-breaker to avoid retries thrashing; coordinate with infra to confirm GPU spare capacity.
- michael/ashley: customer comms + draft credits for impacted tenants.
- jen: compile list of affected accounts + SLA exposure.

michael (support): I'll assemble the comms doc and post to #customer-notices after approval.

diego (runtime): Runtime patch rolled (canary). Early canary shows fewer kernel stalls under the same load. Monitoring for 10m.

ops-bot: ASG scale event completed: +4 GPU nodes in us-west-2.

sam (eng-sre): Post-mitigation status: error rate near baseline, latency improved, throttle is still in place as safety. Recommend we keep throttles for 1h then gradually relax.

laura (oncall): Agreed. We'll leave this as an incident and do a postmortem. Capture timelines + mitigation steps. Diego + Sam, please include telemetry graphs (batcher depth, pod OOMs, kernel errors) in the postmortem.

ashley (support): Customers updated. Two asked for credits—I've started a PR for billing ops referencing incident id 2712345678.

michael (support): Thanks team — logging this thread for the postmortem. Will add convo notes and attach logs to the incident ticket.

laura (oncall): Action items recap (short): 
- diego: owner of postmortem, driver/kernel investigation, runtime patch details (due EOD).
- sam: gateway circuit-breaker proposal + throttle rules change (due tomorrow morning).
- michael/ashley: customer comms + credits reconciliation (due EOD).
- jen: account impact list + SLA note (due EOD).

michael (support): Closing warroom for now — monitoring in #incidents-watch. If error resurges ping laura directly.

laura (oncall): Incident declared resolved at 14:45 UTC for now; we'll treat as mitigated and work on long-term fixes.

ops-bot: Incident 2712345678 status: mitigated -> monitoring."
